record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Maximum degree in the infinite-path regime
record.original_question: For super-linear preferential attachment trees with fitness in the regime where the limiting infinite tree T_infty contains a unique infinite path and every vertex has finite degree, determine the growth rates, as the tree grows, of the maximum degree and of the label of the vertex attaining that maximum degree.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 In the case the infinite tree T∞ contains an infinite path, what are the growth rates of the maximum degree and the label of the vertex that attains the maximum degree?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a super-linear preferential attachment tree with fitness, constructed as follows. Vertices are introduced one at a time and labelled $1,2,3,\dots$. Each vertex $i$ carries an i.i.d. positive fitness $F_i$ drawn from a fixed distribution. Vertex $1$ starts the tree. Given the tree $T_n$ on vertices $\{1,\dots,n\}$, vertex $n+1$ attaches to an existing vertex $v\in T_n$ with probability proportional to $F_v\, w(\deg_{T_n}(v))$, where the weight function $w:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\to(0,\infty)$ is super-linear, i.e.\ $\sum_{k\ge 0} 1/w(k) < \infty$ and $w(k)/k\to\infty$ as $k\to\infty$. Let $T_\infty=\bigcup_n T_n$ be the almost-sure limiting infinite tree.

Assume the fitness distribution and weight function are such that, almost surely, $T_\infty$ contains a unique infinite self-avoiding path starting at vertex $1$ and every vertex of $T_\infty$ has finite degree.

Let $D_n^*=\max_{v\in T_n}\deg_{T_n}(v)$ denote the maximum degree of $T_n$, and let $V_n^*$ denote a vertex of $T_n$ attaining this maximum (label of the maximum-degree vertex).

Determine the almost-sure asymptotic growth rate of $D_n^*$ and of $V_n^*$ as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. Related recent work (e.g., persistence of the maximum degree in preferential attachment trees with vertex death, 2025) addresses neighboring questions but not the growth rates of the maximum degree and its label in the super-linear-with-fitness regime where the limit tree has a unique infinite path with all finite degrees. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Preferential Attachment Trees with Vertex Death: Persistence of the Maximum Degree
status_evidence.snippet: Studies maximum-degree behavior in related preferential attachment tree models, but does not resolve the super-linear-with-fitness infinite-path regime growth rates.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct setting; the specific question is not answered there.

status_evidence.title: Connectivity Transitions in Networks with Super-Linear Preferential Attachment
status_evidence.snippet: Describes structural transitions for super-linear preferential attachment but does not provide growth rates for max degree and its label in the infinite-path regime with fitness.
status_evidence.claim: Background on super-linear regime; does not solve the stated problem.
